claims.text: Locative nouns name directions and positions.
Single-syllable ones mostly attach after a noun (Noun + 上/里/外…).
The forms with 边 can also stand alone as subjects or objects.
Common pattern: 在 + Noun + 上/里/前边…
Note that English prepositions come before the noun, but Chinese locatives come after it.

claims.text: 会 and 能 are modal verbs meaning can, placed before the verb.
Subject + 会/能 + Verb.
会 stresses a learned skill or likelihood; 能 stresses ability, conditions or permission.
Negate with 不会/不能, not 没.

claims.text: 想 and 要 express wishes and intentions before a verb.
Subject + 想/要 + Verb.
想 is a softer would like to; 要 is a firmer want to or will.

claims.text: Question words ask about quantity, choice, place, thing, person and manner.
Question words stay in the position of the answer, so word order does not change as in English.
几 expects a small number and needs a measure word; 多少 works for any number.
Do not add 吗 to a question with one of these words.

别的 means other, and 有的 means some.

claims.text: Basic numerals build numbers, with 十 and 百 as place units and 零 filling an empty place inside a number.
两 replaces 二 before a measure word, while 二 is used in counting, digits and after 十.
半 means half.
半 goes before a measure word, or after one as Number + Measure + 半.

claims.text: Noun measure words come between a number or demonstrative and a noun: Number/这/那 + Measure + Noun.
Each noun takes its own typical measure, such as 本 for books or 杯 for drinks; 个 is the general one.
A number cannot go straight before a noun without a measure word.

本 běn: Classifier for books, periodicals, files. ⇒ all nouns using this classifier

claims.text: Degree adverbs go before adjectives and some verbs to show how much.
Subject + 很/非常/太/真/最 + Adjective.
很 is often a light link with little meaning in adjective sentences.
太 often pairs with 了 at the end to mean too or so.
非常 fēicháng: extremely; very; highly
很 hěn: very; extremely; in a high degree
太 tài: too; so (modifying adjectives; often used with 了 (le) at the end of the sentence for emphasis)

claims.text: The adverbs 都, 一块儿 and 一起 show scope or togetherness.
The adverbs 都, 一块儿 and 一起 go before the verb.
都 means all or both and sums up the people or things before it.
Subject (plural) + 都 + Verb, never before the subject.
一起 and 一块儿 mean together, often after 跟/和 + someone.
都 dū / dōu: all; both (used to indicate that the statement is true for every subject or object); or the entirety of something
一块儿 yīkuàir / yíkuàir: erhua form of 一塊／一块 (yīkuài)
一起 yīqǐ / yìqǐ: together; with

claims.text: Time adverbs go before the verb.
马上 means right away, 先 first, and 有时 sometimes.
在, 正 and 正在 mark an action in progress.
Subject + 在/正在 + Verb (+ 呢).
Do not confuse adverb 在 with the preposition 在 that introduces a place.

先 xiān: first; ahead of time; before; beforehand

claims.text: The adverbs 常, 常常 and 再 show how often something happens or that it happens again; 常 and 常常 mean often and go before the verb.
再 means again for an action not yet done, so it refers to the future.
Negation of 常常 is usually 不常.
常 cháng: often; frequently
常常 chángcháng: frequently; often
再 zài / dài: again; once again; a second time; re-

claims.text: Linking adverbs tie a clause to what came before: 也 means also or too, and 还 adds more or means still.
Both go after the subject, before the verb: Subject + 也/还 + Verb.

claims.text: Negation adverbs go before the verb or adjective.
不 negates habits, wishes, the present and the future, plus most adjectives and 是; 没/没有 negate what happened or existed, and 有 is negated only as 没有.
别 means don't in commands.
别 bié: had better not; do not; don't
不 bù: not; un-; in-; il-; im-; ir-; a(n)-; dys- · no (answer to a yes-no question)

claims.text: The preposition 从 marks a starting point in time or place.
从 + time/place + Verb.
从 often pairs with 到 as 从 A 到 B for a span.
The 从 phrase goes before the verb, not at the end of the sentence.
从 cóng: from (a place or time); since

claims.text: The preposition 在 introduces where an action happens.
Subject + 在 + place + Verb.
The place phrase comes before the verb, unlike English word order.
A plain object noun after 在 usually needs a locative such as 上 or 里 to name a place.
在 zài / zǎi / dài / dǎi: in; at · during; in

Subject + 跟/和 + person + Verb.
跟 and 和 often pair with 一起.

和 hé / hàn / hài: with

A + 比 + B + Adjective.
Do not put 很 or 非常 before the adjective; a difference can follow it instead.
The normal negation is A 没有 B + Adjective, not 不比.
比 bǐ: than; more ... than; -er compared to

和 and 跟 mean and, linking nouns and pronouns but not whole clauses.
还是 means or in questions offering a choice.

claims.text: Two more phrase types: the 的 phrase, where a word plus 的 stands for a noun, meaning the one that; and serial verb phrases, where two or more verbs share one subject in time order.
Pattern: Modifier + 的 for the first; Verb1 + Object + Verb2 for the second.
Noun phrases are phrases headed by or working as nouns, such as a modifier plus noun or a number plus measure word plus noun.
Noun phrases serve as subjects, objects and modifiers.
Noun phrases can sometimes act as predicates for dates, ages or prices.
Verb phrases are phrases headed by verbs, such as verb plus object, adverb plus verb, or verb plus complement.
Verb phrases usually serve as predicates, and can also act as subjects or objects.
Adjective phrases are phrases headed by adjectives, such as degree adverb plus adjective or adjective plus complement.
Adjective phrases serve as predicates without 是, and also as modifiers and complements.

claims.text: Adversative complex sentences contrast the second clause with the first.
Patterns: 虽然……，但是/可是……, or ……，不过…… for a milder turn.
Unlike English, 虽然 and 但是 normally appear together.

links.note: ……，不过…… is a concessive clause pattern
别看 is a colloquial concession like 虽然
尽管 is a stronger, more formal 虽然
虽然 concedes a fact; 即使 a hypothesis
固然 concedes a point before turning
虽说 is a colloquial 虽然
虽 is a written 虽然
然而 is a written 但是

content: （1）不用关联词语（2）用关联词语：如果……，就……；……的话，就……

examples.text: 如果不多运动，你身体就不好。
如果其中一个边的长度又为已知的话，那么其他两条边的长度也就确定。
理论上，如果做的对的话，就检测不到。
如果一个土耳其员工辞职，那么土耳其的工作委员会就会来处理此事。
周二是动员投票的日子，但如果已登记的选民不在名单上就毫无意义了。

claims.text: Hypothetical complex sentences state a supposition and its result.
Patterns: 如果……，就……, or ……的话，就……; 如果 and 的话 can also combine.
就 comes after the subject of the second clause.

links.note: ……的话，就…… is a conditional clause pattern
要是 is a colloquial 如果
假如 is slightly more formal than 如果
倘若 is a written 如果
万一 is for unlikely, unwanted events
一旦 means once something happens

examples.text: 他觉得在生活中遇到困难的时候只要跟我在一起，他就可以克服困难。
后来我发现，只要敢于犯错，进步就会比想象中快得多。
观察空中星宿位置的模样，以占卜未来“天道”的学问，来作为学习基础的制度（不过问身份、只要拥有广泛才能的人就能被选上）。

claims.text: Conditional sentences state a sufficient condition, meaning as long as ... then.
Pattern: 只要 + condition，(Subject) + 就 + result.
只要 sets a minimum condition, unlike 只有……才……, which sets the only condition.

links.note: 只有……才 is necessary; 只要……就 is sufficient

content: （1）不用关联词语（2）用关联词语：因为……，所以……

examples.text: 因为下雨，所以我们没有去公园。
还有因为我是个外国人，所以他每次帮我助我了。
我觉得这可能是因为中国上班比较早，所以一般中国人没有吃早饭的时间。
因为快要上课了，他们害怕迟到，所以他们一边吃着早饭，一边跑去教室。
因为今早要出门，不能用电脑，所以用手机发信息。

claims.text: Cause-and-effect sentences give a reason then a result.
Patterns: 因为……，所以……, or the two clauses with no linking words.
Chinese often uses both words together, unlike English because and so.

links.note: preposition 因为 versus the 因为……所以 clause pair
由于 is more formal and pairs with 因此
之所以 states the effect first, then the cause
既然 cites a known fact; 因为 gives a cause

examples.text: 我们一进游乐园的大门，就开始下雨了。
所以我一有时间，就带着一把钱和一个行李箱去旅行。

claims.text: Compressed sentence meaning as soon as.
Pattern: Subject + 一 + Verb1，(Subject) + 就 + Verb2.
The second action follows the first right away or always happens when the first does.

links.note: 一……就 immediately after; 了……就 after finishing

content: 动词+着 （1）表示状态的持续（2）表示动作的持续

examples.text: 国王光着呢！
我会在这里等着到他回来的。
从什么时候开始您就这里工作着的呢？
他只能看着。
他手里拿着铅笔。

claims.text: Continuous aspect with 着 marks a lasting state, such as wearing something or a door being open, or an ongoing action.
Pattern: Verb + 着.
Negate with 没 + Verb + 着.
For actions in progress, 在 or 正在 is more common.

links.note: 着 shows a lasting state; 在 an ongoing action
continuous aspect is marked by particle 着

examples.text: 我去过罗马。
没有人问过我。
我没去过澳大利亚。
您已经吃过药了吗？
我已经去过还没去过吗？

claims.text: Experiential aspect: 过 after a verb says the action has happened at least once in the past, as an experience.
Pattern: Verb + 过 (+ Object).
Negate with 没（有） + Verb + 过.

links.note: 了1 marks completion; 过 marks past experience
experience aspect is marked by particle 过

examples.text: 那是我第一次坐飞机了。
那就是我的第一次国外旅游。
波因是六个孩子中的第二个。
第二季目前还在进行中吗？
这是你第一次看这部电影吗?

claims.text: Ordinal numbers put 第 before a number, as in first or second.
Pattern: 第 + Number + measure word + Noun.
Some orders skip 第, such as floors, years, dates and family positions like 二哥.

links.note: 第 + numeral is the basic ordinal form

details: 概数表示法1： （1）数词+多+量词（2）数词+量词+多

examples.text: 汤姆昨晚三点多才睡着。
二十分钟多后，我终于到达酒店。

警署内铺有柚木地板，墙身有西式装饰物，勾形中间点的顶层房间，楼底高达十多呎，相信是最高级警官的宴会厅和宿舍。

claims.text: Approximate numbers with 多 meaning a little more than.
Number ending in zero + 多 + measure word leaves the excess in whole units; Number + measure word + 多 leaves only a fraction of one unit.
So 多 before the measure word allows a larger excess than 多 after it.

links.note: 多 after numbers marks approximation

claims.text: 就 used for emphasis, stressing that something is exactly this and nothing else, or a firm decision.
Pattern: Subject + 就 + 是/Verb.
Emphatic 就 is stressed in speech and often answers a doubt.

category: ※“是……的”表示强调（见“是……的”句1和“是……的”句2）)

examples.text: 这是新的。
她是什么时候去蒙古的？
你们是不是在首尔认识的？
你是最高的。
我和她在中学是一个班的。

claims.text: 是……的 used for emphasis: it highlights the time, place, manner or agent of a past action, or affirms the speaker's view.
Pattern: Subject + 是 + stressed part + Verb + 的.
See the 是……的 sentence points for the full patterns.

links.note: 是……的 sentence 1 is one emphatic 是……的
是……的 sentence 2 is one emphatic 是……的

category: 用“好吗/可以吗/行吗/怎么样”提问

examples.text: 老师觉得怎么样？
他是一名很好的老师，对吗？
帮我洗碗好吗？
在去商洛之前，我问了一个朋友商洛怎么样？

claims.text: Tag questions asking for agreement or permission: a statement or suggestion followed by 好吗, 可以吗, 行吗 or 怎么样.
Pattern: Statement, + 好吗/可以吗/行吗/怎么样?
Tag questions soften a request or proposal.

category: 用“什么时候、什么样、为什么、怎么样、怎样”提问

examples.text: 它什么时候到？
老师觉得怎么样？
她是什么时候去蒙古的？
我在等你们。你们什么时候准备好？
从什么时候开始您就这里工作着的呢？

claims.text: Questions with question words: 什么时候 when, 什么样 what kind, 为什么 why, 怎么样 and 怎样 how.
The question word takes the place of the answer, so the word order stays as in a statement.

links.note: 怎样 + verb asks about manner

category: 用“呢”构成的省略式疑问句“代词/名词+呢？”提问

examples.text: 结果呢？

claims.text: Elliptical question: a noun or pronoun + 呢 asks about it in light of what was just said, such as and you?
Without context, it asks where someone or something is.
Pattern: Noun or Pronoun + 呢?

links.note: noun + 呢 questions use the particle 呢

examples.text: 我不知道那是不是真的。
你们是不是在首尔认识的？
让我们来问问这是不是真的。
你们俩之间是不是出现了什么问题？他怎么最近都不来接你了？
因为我的旅行的目的是不是观光，就是帮助别人。

claims.text: Questions with 是不是 seek confirmation of a guess, like isn't it or right.
Pattern: Subject + 是不是 + predicate, or a statement + 是不是?
是不是 can stand before the verb, at the start, or at the end.

links.note: 是不是 is an affirmative-negative question

claims.text: Questions with 吧 ask for confirmation of something the speaker already believes, like right or I suppose.
Pattern: Statement + 吧?
A 吧 question differs from 吗, which asks a neutral yes-no question.

links.note: 吗 is neutral; 吧 seeks confirmation of a guess

examples.text: 该起床了！
他该去火车站了。
他这个时候该到了。
他在该小组中参加了民族调查、民族识别活动。
该分析显示了在一生中吸烟的总数和肿瘤DNA突变的数目之间的直接联系。

claims.text: Pattern for saying it is time to do something, or that something should now happen.
Pattern: (Subject) + 该 + Verb + 了.
The 了 marks the change of situation.

examples.text: 天看起来要下雨了。
他要不行了。
所以我要回家了，可是走路也很难。
因为快要上课了，他们害怕迟到，所以他们一边吃着早饭，一边跑去教室。
快点儿，马上就要超过前面那辆车了。

claims.text: Pattern for an action about to happen, meaning soon or about to.
Pattern: Subject + 要/快要/就要 + Verb + 了.
就要 can take a specific time word before it, but 快要 cannot.

links.note: 将要 is formal; 快要 colloquial soon

examples.text: 我喜欢我的老师。
老师觉得怎么样？
我昨晚睡了五小时。
汤姆不是我们的老师。
我每天运动一小时。

claims.text: Prefixes that attach to the front of a word.
第 + number makes ordinals; 老 + surname or kin term gives a familiar address for someone older or a peer; 小 + surname addresses someone younger.
老 and 小 here carry no literal meaning of old or small.

links.note: semi-prefixes are productive, unlike true prefixes

examples.text: 大家好。
是他们。
他们爱她。
我们在哪儿？
他还在这儿。

claims.text: Suffixes that attach to the end of a word to form nouns.
儿 adds a colloquial or diminutive tone, 家 marks an expert, 们 pluralizes human nouns and pronouns, and 头 and 子 build ordinary nouns.
们 is dropped after a number or quantity word.

links.note: semi-suffixes are productive, unlike true suffixes

examples.text: 但是如果我没有朋友们我不敢想去旅行。
你怎么敢指责我做这种事？我决不会动手打我的儿子。
后来我发现，只要敢于犯错，进步就会比想象中快得多。
如果我选择别人说的那样的旅行方式，并不可能见了很多陌生人到今恐怕不敢跟陌生人打交道。
得了冠军的他张开双臂欢呼，我觉得他一定不敢相信自己眼前的这一切。

claims.text: Modal verb meaning to dare, to have the courage to.
Pattern: Subject + 敢 + Verb.
Negate with 不敢; 没敢 reports a past occasion when someone did not dare.
敢 gǎn: to dare (to); to venture (to)

examples.text: 我需要出去。
你还需要茶吗？
我需要更多时间。
我需要几个人帮我。
她不需要做这个工作。

claims.text: Modal-like verb meaning to need to.
Pattern: Subject + 需要 + Verb phrase.
需要 also takes a plain noun object.
Negate with 不需要, often shortened to 不用 in speech.
需要 xūyào: to need; to require

links.note: 需 is a written 需要

content: 动宾式离合词：帮忙、点头、放假、干杯、见面、结婚、看病、睡觉、洗澡、理发、说话

examples.text: 猫在椅子上睡觉。
她看起来病了。
你在跟我说话吗？
我洗了澡。
我必须帮忙。

claims.text: Verb-object separable words: two-syllable verbs whose second part acts as an object.
Aspect markers, durations and other material go between the parts, as in Verb + 了/过 + amount + Object.
Verb-object separable words usually take no further object; the person is introduced with a preposition such as 跟 or 给.
帮忙 bāngmáng: to help; to give a hand; to do a favor
点头 diǎntóu: to nod (one's head)
放假 fàngjià: to have time off; to go on holidays
干杯 gānbēi: to toast; to drink a toast
见面 jiànmiàn: to meet; to see
结婚 jiéhūn / jiēhūn: to get married; to marry
看病 kànbìng: to see a patient; to treat an illness · to see a doctor
睡觉 shuìjiào: to sleep; to go to bed
洗澡 xǐzǎo / xízǎo: to take a shower or bath; to wash oneself; to bathe
理发 lǐfà / lǐfǎ / lífǎ: to have a haircut; to get a haircut; to cut hair
说话 shuōhuà: to speak; to talk

links.note: 帮忙, 游泳, 跳舞, 跑步 are verb-object separable verbs

content: 动补式离合词：打开、看见、离开、完成

examples.text: 完成了！
我必须离开你。
肉跟凉面离不开。
我看见她在打扫房间。
你有看见过汤姆生气的时候吗？

claims.text: Verb-complement separable words: a verb plus a result or direction element.
得 or 不 can be inserted to express possibility, giving Verb + 得/不 + Complement.
Negate a completed result with 没.
打开 dǎkāi: to open (books, drawers, parcels, doors, etc.) · to switch on (electronics, appliances, etc)
看见 kànjiàn: to see; to sight
离开 líkāi: to leave; to depart
完成 wánchéng: to complete; to finish; to fulfill

content: 疑问代词的非疑问用法 （1）任指用法 ①疑问代词+都……②疑问代词……疑问代词……（2）不定指用法

claims.text: Question words used without asking anything.
Question word + 都/也 + Verb means every or any; two matching question words in two clauses mean whoever, whatever, wherever.
Used alone in a statement, a question word means some or any, as in something or somewhere.

links.note: same question words, but not asking

examples.text: 还有因为我是个外国人，所以他每次帮我助我了。
我完全不负任何责任。
您现在不必购买任何东西。
大概每天有风和美丽的天气。
带着任何的心情，只要有爱，都是你的家

claims.text: Pronouns that pick out every member of a group.
各 + measure or noun means each, often stressing differences.
每 + number + measure means every and usually pairs with 都.
任何 + noun means any and appears mostly with 都/也 in negative or universal statements.
各 gè: each; every (determiner)
各位 gèwèi: ladies and gentlemen; everybody
各种 gèzhǒng: a variety of; all sorts of; all kinds of; a number of; every
每 měi: every; each
任何 rènhé: any; all

content: 把、行、架、群、束、双、台、张、支、只、种

examples.text: 那是只猫还是只狗？
这张票是纸做的。
马是种很有用的动物。
这只手表是叔叔送给我的。
换种方式说。

claims.text: Measure words for nouns, used as Number/这/那 + Measure + Noun.
Each matches a noun class: 把 things with handles, 张 flat sheets, 支 long thin objects, 只 animals or one of a pair, 双 pairs, 台 machines, 架 aircraft, 群 crowds, 束 bunches, 行 lines, 种 kinds.

把 bǎ / bà: Classifier for objects that can be held using handles or knobs, such as guns, chairs, brooms, or umbrellas. ⇒ all nouns using this classifier · Classifier for handfuls of something, such as grains, soil. · Classifier for bundles or bunches.
行 háng: line of objects; row
架 jià: Classifier for planes, large vehicles, radios, etc. ⇒ all nouns using this classifier
群 qún: Classifier for groups of people or animals: group of; flock of; herd of; pack of
束 shù / sù: Classifier for objects in bunches or bundles, such as bouquets of flowers. ⇒ all nouns using this classifier
双 shuāng / shuàng: Classifier for a pair of objects. ⇒ all nouns using this classifier
台 tái: Classifier for machines, vehicles or electronic devices. ⇒ all nouns using this classifier
张 zhāng: Classifier for objects that can be expanded. · Classifier for objects with a flat surface: sheet
支 zhī: Classifier for long, thin objects. ⇒ all nouns using this classifier · Classifier for songs or musical pieces.

只 zhī: Classifier for one of a pair. ⇒ all nouns using this classifier · Classifier for birds and certain animals (especially limbed or small, grabbable by hand). · Classifier for symmetrical body parts, limbs, hands, feet. · Classifier for certain vessels, containers, utensils and objects worn on or grabbable by hand.
种 zhǒng: Classifier for varieties: kind; sort; type ⇒ all nouns using this classifier

把 in another use

examples.text: 从见到她的第一眼开始我就知道我们会有故事发生。

claims.text: Measure words borrowed from body parts to count actions.
Pattern: Verb + number + 顿/口/眼.
顿 counts meals and scoldings or beatings, 口 counts bites or mouthfuls, 眼 counts glances.
顿 dùn: Classifier for meals. · Classifier for beatings, scoldings, etc.: bout
口 kǒu: Classifier for bites or mouthfuls.
眼 yǎn: Classifier for actions of the eye: glance; glimpse

links.note: 口 in another use

examples.text: 那样的事天天都有。

claims.text: A reduplicated measure word means each or every one without exception.
Pattern: AA, usually as subject before 都.
A reduplicated measure word rarely appears as an object.

links.note: measure word reduplication like 个个, 张张
measure word alone versus numeral + measure reduplication

examples.text: 虽然他再不会踢足球，但是他还会教小朋友踢足球。

claims.text: Degree adverbs placed before adjectives and psychological verbs.
比较 means fairly or relatively, 更加 means even more, 还 means still more or reasonably, and 相当 means quite or considerably.
比较 here is an adverb, not the comparison marker 比.

更加 gèngjiā: more; even more
还 hái / huán: even more; indicates an increase from a certain level or a supplement · passably; (surprisingly) quite
相当 xiāngdāng: quite; rather; considerably

claims.text: Adverbs that limit scope.
光, 仅 and 仅仅 mean only or merely; 就 also means only, before the item it limits; 至少 means at least.
光, 仅, 仅仅, 就 and 至少 stand before the verb or the number phrase they restrict.
光 guāng / guǎng: only; alone
仅 jǐn: only; merely
仅仅 jǐnjǐn / jínjǐn: merely; only; just
就 jiù: only; merely; just
至少 zhìshǎo: at least; (to say the) least

content: 本来、才2、曾经、从来、赶紧、赶快、立刻、连忙、始终、已、早已

examples.text: 听说他们下午三点才起来了。
我以前从来没有尝过中餐。
不过我们足足找了半个小时，才找到。
我们谈着谈着，忽然发现了已过关门时间。
最后本来我的朋友不太想去那里却她给我感谢。

claims.text: Time adverbs before the verb.

本来 means originally; 才 means only then, later than expected; 曾经 means once, in the past; 从来 means always or ever, mostly with 不/没; 赶紧, 赶快, 立刻 and 连忙 mean at once; 始终 means from start to finish; 已 and 早已 mean already.
本来 běnlái: originally; the original intent was that
才 cái: only a short while ago; just · only after; only then; not ... until
曾经 céngjīng: once; before; used to; in the past
从来 cónglái: from the past until the present; all along; ever; never (when used with a negated verb)
赶紧 gǎnjǐn / gánjǐn: quickly; hurriedly; immediately; without delay; right away
赶快 gǎnkuài: quickly; hastily; right away; at once
立刻 lìkè: immediately; at once
连忙 liánmáng: promptly; at once; quickly
始终 shǐzhōng: throughout; consistently; from beginning to end
已 yǐ: already; have done something
早已 zǎoyǐ / záoyǐ: for a long time; a long time ago; long ago; long since

claims.text: Frequency adverbs before the verb.
通常 means usually, 往往 means tends to, as a regularity drawn from past experience, and 总/总是 mean always.
往往 describes observed patterns, not future plans or wishes.
通常 tōngcháng: usually; normally; generally; ordinarily
往往 wǎngwǎng / wángwǎng: usually; generally; often; tend to
总 zǒng: always

claims.text: 仅次于X means second only to X.
A + 仅次于 + B.
仅次于X ranks A just below B.
没什么 + Verb + 头儿 means it is not worth doing: there is nothing to gain from the action.
头儿 turns the verb into a noun of value.

links.note: both say something is not worth doing
rhetorical 有什么 + verb + 头儿 means 没什么

claims.text: 没什么好 + Verb + 的 means there is nothing worth doing about it.
没什么好 + Verb + 的 dismisses something as not worth the trouble.

links.note: 没什么好 + verb + 的 is one form of it

claims.text: 莫过于…… means nothing is more than or nothing exceeds.
A + 莫过于 + B.
莫过于…… presents B as the most extreme case.
你说你一个X，…… means look at you, a X, and yet ….
你说你一个X，…… criticizes behavior unfitting for the listener's role.
视……而定 means depending on or to be decided by.
视 + condition + 而定.
视……而定 is formal.
谈何…… means how can one speak of, implying it is very hard.
谈何 + 容易/Noun.
谈何…… is literary.
想X之所想，急X之所急 means to think what someone thinks and worry about what worries them.
想X之所想，急X之所急 describes deep care for others' needs.
向……致以…… means to extend or express something to someone formally.
向 + Person + 致以 + 问候/感谢/敬意.
向……致以…… is ceremonial.
有何X means what X is there.
有何 + Noun?
有何X is a literary question, often rhetorical.
有什么 + Verb + 头儿 means what is the point of doing it.
有什么 + Verb + 头儿 is a rhetorical question dismissing an action as worthless.

links.note: rhetorical 有什么 + verb + 头儿 means 没什么

claims.text: （在）……之余 means in the time left over from or in addition to.
(在) + activity + 之余, + another activity.
（在）……之余 is formal.
值此……之际，…… means on the occasion of.
值此 + event + 之际, + greeting or statement.
值此……之际，…… is ceremonial.
A + Adjective + 于/过 + B is a formal comparison meaning A is more … than B.
于 is written style; 过 is literary and terse.

links.note: 于/过 comparison is formal; 比 is everyday

claims.text: 一来……，二来……，三来…… means firstly …, secondly …, thirdly ….
一来……，二来……，三来…… lists reasons.
Mostly in speech.

links.note: both list reasons or aspects in sequence
一则 is more formal than 一来

claims.text: 一则……，二则……，三则…… means firstly …, secondly …, thirdly …, listing reasons.
In formal style.

links.note: 一则 is more formal than 一来

claims.text: 所谓……，就是…… means what is called X is simply Y.
所谓 + term, 就是 + explanation.
所谓……，就是…… defines or reframes a term.

links.note: 所谓……就是…… defines a term

claims.text: X（倒）是X（了），…… concedes a point by repeating a word, then turns to a contrast: X is X all right, but ….
X（倒）是X（了），…… is spoken.

links.note: the same concessive X是X frame; 倒 and 了 optional

claims.text: 别看……，…… means despite appearances or don't judge by.
The first clause gives what is seen, the second the contrary fact.
别看 biékàn: in spite of; despite; for all that

links.note: 别看 is a colloquial concession like 虽然

claims.text: 虽说……，但/可…… means although.
In a spoken style.
The first clause concedes a fact, and the second states the contrast.

links.note: 虽说……，但/可…… concession

claims.text: 凡……（者），均（可）…… means anyone who … may ….
凡……（者），均（可）…… states a rule for every member of a class.
In formal notices.

links.note: 凡……均 is the formal 凡是……都

claims.text: 假若 and 假使 mean if.
In formal or literary style.
假若/假使 + condition, + result.
假若 and 假使 state a hypothesis.
假若 jiǎruò: if; supposing
假使 jiǎshǐ / jiáshǐ: if; in case

links.note: 假若 and 假使 are formal versions of 假如

claims.text: 纵然 and 纵使 mean even if.
纵然/纵使 + condition, 也 + result.
纵然 and 纵使 are literary.
Introduce an extreme hypothesis that does not change the result.

links.note: 纵然……也 is the 纵然 half of 纵然/纵使

claims.text: ……不说，还…… means not only that, but also.
The first clause names something, 不说 sets it aside as granted, and 还 adds a further point.
还 hái / huán: even more; indicates an increase from a certain level or a supplement

links.note: both add a further point

claims.text: ……尚且……，（更）何况…… means even X is so, let alone Y.
The first clause gives a case that should be easier, and the second an even clearer one.

links.note: 尚且 adds the first clause to 何况

claims.text: 为（了）……起见 means for the sake of.
为(了) + purpose + 起见, + action.
为（了）……起见 is formal.
States why a precaution is taken.

links.note: 为……起见 is formal purpose framing

claims.text: 非得……才…… means only if … will …, stressing a necessary condition.
非得 + condition + 才 + result.

links.note: both stress necessity

claims.text: 任……也…… means no matter how, in a contracted sentence.
任 + condition + 也 + result.
任……也…… shows the result does not change.

links.note: 任……也 means whatever happens

claims.text: A multiple-layer coordinate complex sentence has a parallel relation at its top level, with other relations nested inside the parts.
A multiple-layer contrast complex sentence has a contrast at its top level, with other relations nested inside the parts.
A multiple-layer hypothetical complex sentence has a hypothesis at its top level, with other relations nested inside the parts.
A multiple-layer causal complex sentence has cause and effect at its top level, with other relations nested inside the parts.
A multiple-layer progressive complex sentence has a progression at its top level, with other relations nested inside the parts.
Sentences in a paragraph can follow time order, describing events as they happened.
Time words and connectors such as 先, 然后 and 最后 mark the sequence.
Sentences can follow spatial order, describing a scene from one place to another, such as near to far or top to bottom.
Locative words mark the positions.
Sentences can follow logical order, such as cause to effect or general to specific.
Connectors make the reasoning explicit.
Topic extension: a paragraph develops one topic by adding detail, examples or explanation.
The topic stays the same across sentences.
Topic shift: a paragraph moves from one topic to another.
Markers such as 至于 or 另外 signal the change.
Anaphoric omission: an element mentioned earlier is left out in later sentences, because the reader can recover it from the preceding context.

links.note: ellipsis of a part already mentioned

claims.text: Cataphoric omission: an element is left out in an earlier clause and only named later.
The reader recovers it from what follows.

links.note: ellipsis of a part mentioned later
